summary: A Buddhist studies scholar, Shoyu Hanayama studied at the University of Tokyo (~1951–1958). He served as vice president at Musashino University (~1966–1995) and chairperson of the Society for the Promotion of Buddhism (~1988–1995).

Shozen Kumoi was a Buddhist studies and Indology scholar who studied at Otani University and under Erich Frauwallner. He held posts at Otani University (1948–1981; emeritus ~1986–2017), Bukkyo University, Kyoto University, and the University of Vienna.

Shri Krishna Saksena worked in philosophy and Indology, and his students included John M. Koller. He served as a professor at both the University of Lucknow and the University of Hawaiʻi (attested 2016).
Shri Krishna Sharma was a scholar of Indology and linguistics who taught Dieter Schuh. He founded the Hindu Maha Sabha and DAV College, Suva.

An Indologist, Shridhar Ramakrishna Bhandarkar was assistant to the professor of Sanskrit at Deccan College (1884). He later served as professor of Sanskrit at Elphinstone College and permanent professor of Sanskrit at Wilson College, Mumbai.

Shridhar Tryambak Pathak worked in Indology. He held appointments as a Shastri at Deccan College Post-Graduate and Research Institute (attested 1921) and as a Sanskrit teacher at Elphinstone College (attested 1927).

An Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar, Shrikant S. Bahulkar studied under Vasudev Vishwanath Gokhale. He served as chief editor at the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies and as professor at Tilak Maharashtra Vidyapeeth (attested 2000–2007).

Shrinarayan Mishra, a scholar of Indology, linguistics, and philosophy, studied under Anantalal Thakur. He spent his career at Banaras Hindu University as lecturer in Sanskrit (attested 1971), reader (attested 1985), and professor emeritus (attested 2010).

An Indologist and philosopher, Belvalkar studied under Kashinath Bapu Pathak. He was professor of Sanskrit at Deccan College (~1914–1937), secretary (~1918–1943) and Mahabharata general editor (1948–1961) at BORI, and general secretary of the All-India Oriental Conference.

An Indologist and religious studies scholar, Shrivatsa Goswami studied philosophy at Banaras Hindu University, where he later taught. He founded Sri Caitanya Prema Samsthana (1972) and held appointments at Harvard University and the Vrindaban Research Institute.

Specializing in Buddhist studies and philosophy, Shu-chen Chen earned a PhD at the University of Virginia, where she was also a teaching assistant (1996). Her doctoral supervisors were Jeffrey Hopkins and Karen Christina Lang.

Shu-fen Chen is a scholar of linguistics and Indology who studied at National Tsing Hua University and completed doctoral work under Hans Henrich Hock. She served as a professor at National Tsing Hua University (attested 2010).

Shubhachandra is an Indology scholar who served as a professor at Karnatak University (attested 2001) and was affiliated with the Department of Jainology and Prakrits at the University of Mysore (attested 2002).

A Buddhist studies and sinology scholar, Shudo Ishii studied under Shigeo Kamata and earned his BA and doctorate from Komazawa University. He held multiple faculty roles at Komazawa (1971–2014) and served as acting head at Matsugaoka Bunko.

Shuhong Chang worked in history, archaeology, sinology, and Buddhist studies. Educated in Lyon and Paris, he taught at Zhejiang University and the National Beiping Art Academy, and served as director and honorary director of the Dunhuang Academy (1942–1985).
Shuichi Maida was a Buddhist studies scholar. He studied at Kyoto University and studied under Haya Akegarasu.

A Buddhist studies scholar, Shuji Takayama served as an adjunct lecturer at Ryukoku University (2003), commissioned researcher at Bukkyo University (2003), visiting researcher at Kyushu Ryukoku Junior College (2006), and researcher at Musashino University (2006).
Shujiro Shimada was a scholar of Japanology, sinology, and history/archaeology. He studied at Kyoto University (~1928–1931) and later held a post at Princeton University (~1962–1975).

Shujun Motegi, a scholar of Indology and philosophy, studied under Kamlesh Dutt Tripathi at Banaras Hindu University and earned an MA from Kyoto University. He served as professor of ethics at Shinshu University (attested 1998, 2010).

A Buddhist studies scholar, Shuken Ito completed undergraduate and doctoral studies at Komazawa University. He served there as research assistant (attested 1973, 1976) and professor (from 1991), and was a visiting professor at Aichi Gakuin University (1998).
